judged_text: deleteEvent has the same falsy-value tautology - when externalCalendarId is null it looks for a destination whose externalId equals null, which never matches, so calendarId resolves to undefined. Cancelling any booking with a destination calendar but a reference lacking externalCalendarId calls calendar.events.delete with an undefined required calendarId; the deletion fails and the Google Calendar event, with all attendee invites, stays live on hosts' calendars after the booking is cancelled - orphaned external data with no cleanup path.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now derive the calendar id with a tautological/incorrect fallback: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is `null/undefined`, the `.find(...)` compares against that same `null/undefined` value, so it won’t select the intended destination calendar (e.g., the first/main one) and resolves to `undefined`. This can cause Google update/delete calls to target no calendar id (or an unintended default if later fallback exists), meaning cancellation may fail to delete the actual event when references lack `externalCalendarId`.
